A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RDT-1B and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-I. The complete material supports reliable matching and comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original real-robot experiments across seven tasks, success rates in Table 3, ablations in Table 2 and Figure 4, and training diagnostics and qualitative results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and appendix results, and additionally displays the full-RDT training-loss trajectory in Figure 4a.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-C retain the same diffusion objective, action chunking, encoders, normalization, MLP decoder, alternating condition injection, and unified action space. Rewritten explanations do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 46 pre-training datasets, 6K+ fine-tuning episodes, and seven evaluation tasks. Coverage of unseen objects and scenes, instruction following, few-shot learning, and dexterity is unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain ACT, OpenVLA, Octo, and the same RDT ablations. ACT remains excluded from instruction-following comparisons. Figure 4a adds the proposed model's trace rather than a new competing method.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices D-H retain the same preprocessing, training budgets, checkpoints, metrics, trial counts, and baseline fine-tuning procedures. The additional Figure 4a trace does not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 4a strengthens the existing normalization-stability analysis by adding full RDT's loss curve alongside the curve without QKNorm and RMSNorm. The other architectural ablations, Table 2 analyses, and appendix diagnostics are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same trial-count reporting and point success rates. Neither introduces confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed variability estimates; the added loss curve is not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 4a newly reports the full-RDT loss trajectory. Success rates in Tables 2-3, aggregate results in Figure 1, including RDT's 68.2%, and appendix results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation, diffusion equations, objective, action-chunk definitions, and unified-space specification are unchanged. The new footnote defining 'unseen' restates v1's inline explanation; no mathematical argument or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about model scale, unified action representation, generalization, instruction following, few-shot learning, and dexterity. Introduction edits preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 narrows the camera shortcut-learning explanation: v1 says ignoring wrist views loses depth perception, while v2 describes neglecting wrist-camera details without that specific causal assertion. Other result interpretations and applicability boundaries remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement changes from supplementary code and a promised future release to a direct repository link and a reported release of code, weights, and fine-tuning data. Technical configurations and implementation appendices remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 4.1 correct DiT attribution from Xie et al. (2020) to Peebles and Xie (2023). Both works were already in the bibliography; the broader literature coverage and research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction and multimodal-encoding explanation receive localized rewrites, with additional examples, a footnote, and typo corrections. Affiliations, corresponding-author information, and acknowledgments are updated; the section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 4a gains the RDT curve and a legend. Conference headers and modest text reflow alter page presentation, while the remaining figures and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The added full-RDT curve makes the normalization-stability argument easier to assess. Corrected DiT attribution and the direct repository link with reported artifact release also improve accuracy and access documentation. These are limited gains; the core experiments, benchmark results, and technical appendices remain unchanged.
